source: the editor's session of 8 Oct 2026: decisions D1–D9 of the review packet of 5 Oct, the digest intake of the 2026-10-08 issue (industry stream and paper channel), the WP2 pilot tagging of every two-qubit error figure (data/register/machine-2q-classes.csv) and the corrections it found

items.note: DEPLOYED → DEMONSTRATED (25 Sep 2025) with 64 qubits — IonQ ran #AQ 64 on a "Tempo development system" in one ion chain, while its own systems page lists the 100-qubit Tempo product for "Late 2026" with 100 "Target qubits" and 99.9% "Target fidelity", which move to the roadmap; no two-qubit error is published for the device; the "256" belongs to the separate Superion 256 row; the 99.99% in IonQ's 8-K exhibits is Oxford Ionics' two-ion result. The editor's decision D1 (option A), 8 Oct 2026.

fields.roadmap: fault tolerance 2028-2029; 256 logical qubit system by 2030 (technology page, read Oct 2026)

items.note: «our path to fault tolerance leverages these achievements and aims to deliver a 256 logical qubit system by 2030» (digest intake 2026-10-08, the industry stream)

fields.demonstrated_algorithms: analog optimisation and materials Hamiltonians; simulation of the magnetic material TmMgGaO₄ with up to 256 atoms on Orion Beta QPUs, compared against laboratory measurements (with academic partners; reported 24 Sep 2026)

items.note: «Pasqal and its academic partners used up to 256 atoms on Pasqal’s Orion Beta QPUs to simulate the magnetic material TmMgGaO₄ and compared the results against laboratory measurements» (digest intake 2026-10-08, the industry stream)

fields.access: orders open; a Superion 256 planned for deployment with an SDT customer in South Korea (announced 21 Sep 2026, no date)

items.note: «Deployment will bring the first IonQ Superion 256 system and first silicon-vacancy quantum memory module to South Korea» (digest intake 2026-10-08, the industry stream)

2026-09-08 — D-Wave Quantum executed a definitive agreement with the U.S. Department of Commerce giving it access to up to $100 million of CHIPS and Science Act funding for R&D on its annealing and gate-model systems; the Department receives a minority, non-controlling equity stake. [SEC 8-K exhibit]

2026-09-08 — Quantinuum finalized an agreement with the U.S. Department of Commerce's CHIPS Research and Development Office for $100 million in federal funding under the CHIPS and Science Act, for R&D and U.S. quantum semiconductor manufacturing capabilities needed to deploy large-scale, fault-tolerant trapped-ion quantum computers. [SEC 8-K exhibit]

Pasqal's H1-2026 results (Form 6-K exhibit, 24 Sep 2026) report defect-free registers of 1,024 atoms on a redesigned cryogenic platform — a laboratory result, not a register device (Orion is cryogenics-free; no machine, gate or paper named); and up to 256 atoms used on Orion Beta QPUs in one TmMgGaO4 simulation — the Orion row keeps 140 qubits (per-site systems of 140 and 200), the 256-atom run is in its prose.

Quantum Art's first-generation QaaS system "Montage" (up to 50 qubits; the owner's roadmap: "2025 Launching our 1st generation QaaS system of up to 50 qubits (Montage Series)"); the QaaS access text moves here from the Perspective row. Digest intake 2026-10-08 (catalogue audit); the editor's tier.
